segments: The tenth jubilee.
Arab kings.
And they heard again that the Tatars had left Khorasan (Khwarazm?) and crossed the Gihon to the east,
and Jalal al-Din led those who were with him,
and they departed from India and came to Shiraz.
And the Atabeg Sa'd, the lord of Shiraz, sent him an abundance of wealth, male slaves, and female slaves.
And from there they came to Isfahan.
And in the year six hundred and twenty of the Arabs, Sultan 'Ala al-Din took a strong fortress on the shore of the Adranus {OCR?} Sea (the Mediterranean),
and he named it after his own name, 'Ala'iyya ('Alaya?).
Concerning {OCR?} the murder of {OCR?} Thomas in Baghdad.
And in this same year, on the twenty-sixth {OCR?} of Jumada {OCR?} the first, which is the fifth month of the Arabs, on Thursday night,
there was killed the glorious physician, famous for his virtues, Amin al-Dawla Abu al-Karam Sa'id bar Thomas of Baghdad, from among our own Jacobites.
For he was skilled in medicine,
trustworthy in his conduct,
discerning, generous, and a fine mediator in supplying the needs of the destitute,
answering their requests,
and accomplishing their affairs.
And for all this he was beloved and honored by Caliph al-Nasir, and became great,
so that to him was entrusted the entire administration of his kingdom, and of his sons, his daughters, and his wives.
And because Caliph al-Nasir in the end of his days had his eyes weakened,
and was no longer able to see to write secret matters to the vizier,
there was found a certain woman {OCR?} in Baghdad
whose name was Sitt Nasim,
who wrote a handwriting that was not distinguishable at all from that of the caliph.
And al-Nasir brought her to himself,
and revealed his secrets to her.
And everything that he wished to write,
he told her to write.
And whenever the writings reached the vizier, he thought that they were the very shapes of the fingers of al-Nasir himself,
because he concealed his blindness even from the vizier.
And when things had remained like this for some time,
a certain eunuch whose name was Taj al-Din Rashiq conspired with her,
and they would write whatever they wished in the name of the caliph to the vizier,
and he would fulfill it.
And on one of the days, that vizier, Mu'ayyad al-Din bar Qasimi, wrote to the caliph concerning a certain matter,
and an answer came out to him that was confused and disordered.
And suspicion arose in him concerning this,
and he apprehended the glorious Amin al-Dawla...
